interest in the synthesis of functionalized (benzo)furans

divergent method involving two inexpensive Lewis acids for
the construction of diverse C2-functionalized furanyl/pyrrolyl

Scheme 6 Proposed mechanism.
A plausible reaction mechanism for this cascade protocol
has been proposed in Scheme 6. Initially, β-ketoallene 1 is acti-
vated by Lewis acid catalysts to form a dual-coordinated
adduct I with the allene moiety and the oxygen of the carbonyl
group, which display distinct activity depending on the cata-
lytic metals. The catalytic zinc center might slightly favour
coordination to the allene moiety over the oxygen, thus trigger-
ing an intramolecular 5-exo-trig cyclization to form an
oxonium intermediate II-a. In the absence of nucleophiles, the
reaction is almost shut down with a large amount of
β-ketoallene 1 being preserved, and no Friedel–Crafts cycliza-
tion product 12 is observed. Therefore, we postulated that the
resulting II-a is sluggish to undergo fragmentation to form the
acyl cation II-b. If a very small amount of transient II-b is
formed, it would be trapped by excessive external nucleophiles
in an irreversible manner, thus driving the processes toward
the desired product. In contrast, the bismuth catalyst might
have a stronger afinity to oxygen than the allene moiety,
resulting in a more active carbonyl group, which is sub-
sequently captured by aniline to give geminal amino alcohol
III and then undergoes bismuth-assisted dehydration to form
ketimine IV.<sup>12a,15</sup> Finally, the more nucleophilic ketimine
engages the activated allene moiety through a similar 5-exo-trig
cyclization, followed by a fragmentation–trapping process to
furnish pyrrole 4.
Conclusions
In summary, we have developed an operationally simple,
unified strategy for the synthesis of diversely substituted
C2-furan or pyrrole carboxylic acid derivatives via a cascade
reaction from simple and readily available/preparable starting
materials. The cascade is proposed to go through consecutive
processes of cyclization, ring fragmentation, aromatization
and an
\mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { N } } 1
reaction involving acyl cation species as the
key intermediate. This catalytic protocol, characterized by in-
expensive catalysts and high atom economy, provides access
to a wide variety of tri- and tetrasubstituted furan/pyrrole
derivatives in excellent yields. In addition, the cyclization–
fragmentation strategy was studied for its generality and scal-
ability by carrying out gram-scale synthesis and downstream
synthetic transformations. This methodology might also
provide a potential synthetic route to tetrasubstituted furan
fatty acids.
